title: Size and timescale of epidemics in the SIR framework
experiment: Halving the contact rate α and doubling the removal rate β flatten the SIR peak I(t)/N to the same height, but the reader sees the β route reach its peak and fall below the safety level in about half the time. This is the scaling law of Eq. (23) (II.3, Table 1).
archetype_reason: the SIR equations (1) are ODEs integrated in time, and the claims concern the peak height and the timing of I(t)

fixed.equations: dS/dt = -alpha S I; dI/dt = alpha S I - beta I; dR/dt = beta I

source.quote: the parameter $\alpha$ corresponds to a contact rate (also called infection rate)
The parameter $\beta$ is a removal rate; more precisely, it is the inverse of the typical removal time

metrics.name: peak_frac
metrics.label: peak infectives
metrics.meaning: maximum over the run of I(t)/N

metrics.name: peak_day
metrics.label: peak day
metrics.meaning: time t in days at which I(t) attains its maximum over the run

metrics.name: t_safe
metrics.label: time to safe level
metrics.meaning: first time t after peak_day at which I(t)/N < 1e-4; equals the run length (300 days) if never reached

reproduce.claim: Raising γ twofold by halving α (social distancing) lowers the peak to about 0.30 N, but the peak arrives near day 82 and the safe level near day 189.

source.quote: Actions reducing $\gamma$ by the same factor through action on the different parameters produce the same epidemic peak level, but with a substantially different dynamics.

contrast.claim: Raising γ by the same factor through doubling β (early detection and isolation) gives the same peak height, but the peak and the safe level both arrive in roughly half the time.

source.quote: containment measures with $\lambda=2$ reduce by a half both the time needed for the epidemic to reach the peak and the whole time-span of the epidemic

fallback.title: Size and timescale of epidemics in the SIR framework
fallback.experiment: Changing α and β moves the epidemic threshold γ = β/α. The reader sees the predicted peak I*/N from Eq. (8) shrink as γ grows, and drop to zero once γ exceeds N.
fallback.archetype_reason: the peak height is a closed-form function of γ (Eq. 8), and γ is set by the configuration of α and β

fixed.peak_formula: I*/N = 1 - g - g*ln(1/g) with g = gamma/N if g < 1, else 0
